Thanks for flagging — quick internal note on root cause and a persistent fix.

Root cause: Our Calendly account global timezone is locked to US/Pacific (legacy setting from when the team was US-centric). Calendly will send invites with timezone offsets, but some calendar clients (older Outlook versions, and a few corporate Google Workspace settings) ignore Calendly's conversion and render the event at the organizer timezone. That produces the "11:00 on our calendar, 02:00 on theirs" symptom. DST transitions amplify the confusion across US/EU when DST change dates differ.

Immediate action (what I'll do now):
1) Switch the Calendly org default timezone to "Automatically detect invitee timezone" (Calendly support article: https://calendly.help/articles/region-settings) — this will take effect for new event types.
2) Create region-specific event types (EU / US / APAC) for customer-facing reps so invite metadata includes explicit TZ IDs (e.g., Europe/Paris).
3) For this thread: I will mark the existing event as "manual override" and confirm the .ics from Priyom is authoritative. Marissa, please follow up to update the GreenFin calendaring event and add a note about the join link and VPN pre-check.

Longer term: we should add a short line in our outbound scheduling CTAs: "Select the time that matches your local timezone — if the invite looks off, rebook using this Chili Piper link." That reduces friction for enterprise prospects in APAC/EU.

Marissa — can you take the ticket to update the org settings and create the EU event type? ETA EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Sales Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
